significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that "language-specific input encoding and output decoding wrap this shared store" and that cross-lingual factual failures arise despite preserved mid-layer knowledge—a form-(ii) causal mechanism with an ordering of input, storage, and output computations, rather than a mere existence claim. It establishes both a behavioral phenomenon (facts remain decodable when the surface answer is wrong) and a mechanistic decomposition that would constrain explanations of the language-dependent recall failures documented in X-FACTR (Jiang et al., 2020) and would inform whether multilingual knowledge editing should target storage or language interfaces. Verified false, it would rule out the stated general shared-store/access-only account and leave genuinely language-dependent storage as necessary for at least some failures; the branches are distinguishable, although "largely language-agnostic" leaves the exact prevalence threshold underspecified. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the broad assigned topic alone does not imply this specific cross-lingual stage ordering or the claim that inaccessible facts remain internally available.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "storage-sharing index," the "verbalization-gap," and the distinction among "input-store-output" failure locations, which downstream researchers could use as diagnostics and as a design rule for deciding whether to strengthen language interfaces or reteach facts. These are principally post-hoc handles because they diagnose an existing wrong answer rather than forecasting failure before a query is attempted, though the conclusion could affect multilingual training and knowledge-editing choices. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction would survive as a relation—mid-layer cross-language decodability should remain higher than successful verbalization and should persist on surface-wrong cases—rather than merely supplying an unconstrained search procedure; its asserted scope covers factual associations across languages and relations, with uptake among interpretability researchers and multilingual-model auditors or builders. The topic-substitution check fails to retain the score: deleting the shared-store hypothesis also deletes the transferable diagnostic relation and all three named handles, so the reach is attributable to the claim rather than to the general knowledge-retrieval topic.
